en: vt. to put something inside something else; to add something to a piece of writing; vi. to be put into something; n. something that is put inside something else, such as a page in a book
ex: Insert the key into the lock and turn it to the right.
把鑰匙插入鎖孔並向右轉。

en: n. a careful examination of something to check its quality or condition; an official visit to check that something is working properly; a close look at something
ex: The factory passed the safety inspection last week.
工廠上週通過了安全檢查。

en: n. a feeling of enthusiasm or a new idea that makes you want to do something; a person or thing that gives you ideas; the act of breathing in
ex: The beautiful scenery gave her inspiration for the painting.
美麗的風景給了她畫這幅畫的靈感。

en: vt. to put a piece of equipment or software in place so that it is ready to use; to officially put someone in a new position; to place something in a particular position
ex: The technician installed a new air conditioner in the office.
技師在辦公室裝了一台新冷氣機。

en: n. a natural way of behaving or reacting that is not learned; a natural ability to know something without thinking; a. filled with something
ex: Birds fly south for the winter by instinct.
鳥類本能地飛往南方過冬。

en: vt. to teach someone a skill or subject; to give someone an order or tell them what to do; to give someone information
ex: The coach instructed the players to run ten laps.
教練指示球員跑十圈。

en: n. a person who teaches a particular skill or sport; a university teacher below the rank of professor
ex: Our driving instructor was very patient.
我們的駕訓教練很有耐心。

en: n. a rude remark or action that offends someone; vt. to speak or behave rudely to someone; to hurt someone's feelings
ex: She took his remark as an insult.
她把他的話當作一種侮辱。

en: n. a person who uses their mind to study, think and talk about ideas; a. relating to the ability to think and understand; involving a lot of thought
ex: The professor is a leading intellectual in the field.
那位教授是該領域的頂尖知識分子。

en: n. the ability to learn and understand things; secret information about an enemy or competitor; information; the people who collect such information
ex: She has a high level of intelligence and learns very fast.
她智力很高，學東西很快。

en: a. involving a lot of work or effort in a short period of time; giving a lot of attention to one thing; (of farming) using a lot of labor or fertilizer to produce more
ex: She took an intensive course in Japanese for six weeks.
她上了六週的日語密集課程。

en: n. a plan or purpose in your mind; what you want to do; the reason why someone does something
ex: She had no intention of quitting her job.
她沒有辭掉工作的打算。

en: vi. to communicate or work with someone; (of two things) to have an effect on each other; to react with another substance; n. a short performance between two parts of a play
ex: Children learn by interacting with each other.
孩子們透過互相互動來學習。

en: n. the way in which two or more people or things communicate or react to each other; an effect that two things have on each other
ex: Social interaction is important for children's development.
社交互動對兒童發展很重要。

en: vi. to get involved in a situation that does not concern you; to prevent something from happening or developing normally; to have a bad effect on something
ex: Please don't interfere in my private life.
請不要干涉我的私生活。

en: a. having a close and friendly relationship with someone; private and personal; (of knowledge) very detailed and thorough; vt. to suggest something indirectly; n. a close friend
ex: They have been intimate friends since childhood.
他們從小就是親密的朋友。

en: vt. to enter a country with an army in order to take control of it; to enter a place in large numbers; to disturb someone's private life
ex: The army invaded the neighboring country at dawn.
軍隊在黎明時入侵了鄰國。

en: n. the act of entering a country with an army to take control of it; the act of entering a place in large numbers; the act of disturbing something private
ex: The invasion of the island began at midnight.
島嶼的入侵行動在午夜開始。

en: vt. to include something as a necessary part; to make someone take part in something; to connect someone with a crime or something bad; (involvement) the act of taking part in something
ex: The project involves a lot of teamwork.
這個專案需要大量團隊合作。

en: vt. to separate something or someone from others; to find the cause of a problem by separating it from other things; n. a separated group
ex: Sick patients are isolated from other people in the hospital.
生病的病人在醫院裡與其他人隔離。

en: n. an important topic that people are discussing or arguing about; a problem or worry; a copy of a newspaper or magazine published on a particular day; the act of giving something out officially; vt. to officially give something to someone; vi. to come out of a place
ex: Climate change is a major issue of our time.
氣候變遷是我們這個時代的重大議題。

en: n. a feeling of anger and unhappiness because someone has something that you want; a feeling of being afraid that someone you love may prefer someone else
ex: He felt a pang of jealousy when he saw her with another man.
他看到她和另一個男人在一起時感到一陣嫉妒。

en: n. a container with a lid, a spout and a handle, used for boiling water; (British) an electric device for boiling water; a large metal pot
ex: She put the kettle on to make tea.
她把水壺放上去燒水泡茶。

en: n. hard physical work; work or effort of any kind; workers as a group, especially in industry; the process of giving birth to a child; vi. to work hard; vt. to explain something in too much detail
ex: The labor of building the pyramid took twenty years.
建造金字塔的勞動花了二十年。

en: n. an easily seen object that helps people recognize a place; a famous building or place; an important event or achievement in history; a stone that marks a boundary
ex: The Eiffel Tower is a famous landmark in Paris.
艾菲爾鐵塔是巴黎著名的地標。
ph: 具有里程碑意義的裁決
具有里程碑意義的案例

en: n. everything you can see when you look across an area of land; a painting of natural scenery; the appearance of a particular situation; vt. to improve a piece of land by planting trees and flowers
ex: The mountain landscape was breathtaking.
山景令人屏息。

en: vi. to bend your body towards or against something; to rest against something; to depend on someone or something; a. thin in a healthy way; (of meat) containing little fat; n. meat with little fat
ex: She leaned against the wall and closed her eyes.
她靠著牆壁閉上眼睛。

en: a. having a lot of knowledge from studying; (of work) showing great knowledge; (past tense and past participle of learn)
ex: He is a learned man who has read thousands of books.
他是個博學的人，讀過數千本書。

en: n. a speech given to a group of people to teach them about a subject; a long angry talk to someone about their behavior; vt. to give a speech to an audience; to tell someone angrily that they have done something wrong; vi. to give a lecture
ex: The professor gave an interesting lecture on ancient history.
教授發表了一場關於古代歷史的有趣演講。

en: n. a colored substance used for making your lips look redder or more attractive; a stick of this substance
ex: She applied some red lipstick before the party.
她在派對前塗了一些紅色口紅。

en: n. books, plays and poems that are considered to have artistic value; written information about a particular subject; books or articles that are produced to promote something
ex: She studies English literature at university.
她在大學主修英國文學。

en: vt. to make something less tight; to untie something; to make rules less strict; vi. to become loose or less tight
ex: He loosened his tie after a long day at work.
他在忙碌了一天後鬆開了領帶。

en: a. always supporting a person, organization or country; faithful and reliable; showing strong support or trust
ex: The dog was loyal to his owner for twelve years.
那隻狗忠於主人十二年。

en: a. very comfortable and expensive; providing great pleasure or luxury; enjoying pleasures and comforts
ex: They stayed in a luxurious hotel by the sea.
他們住在海邊的豪華飯店。

en: n. a very expensive and comfortable way of living; something expensive that is not necessary but gives you pleasure; a. expensive and of very high quality
ex: Living in luxury doesn't always bring happiness.
生活奢華不一定帶來幸福。

en: n. products such as lipstick and powder that people put on their faces; the way something is made up; a person's character or personality; an exam that someone takes again
ex: She spends a lot of time putting on her makeup every morning.
她每天早上花很多時間化妝。

en: vt. to make goods in large numbers using machines; to invent a story or excuse; n. the act of making goods; a product made in a factory
ex: The factory manufactures car parts for several companies.
這家工廠為好幾家公司製造汽車零件。

en: n. the state of being fully grown or developed; the time when someone is an adult; the time when an insurance policy or investment pays out
ex: He showed great maturity for someone so young.
對這麼年輕的人而言，他表現出很高的成熟度。

en: a. able to be measured; important enough to be noticed; likely to happen soon
ex: There has been a measurable improvement in her health.
她的健康出現了可衡量的改善。

en: a. relating to machines; done by a machine; done without thinking, as if you were a machine; relating to the science of mechanics
ex: The car has a mechanical problem and needs to be repaired.
這輛車有機械故障，需要修理。
